4.3.1.10.3 Queueing of mode switches
The communication of mode switch notifications is typically event driven. Ac-
cordingly, RTE offers a similar queueing mechanism as for the ’queued’ sender receiver
communication, described above.
[SWS_Rte_02718]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107
⌈The RTE shall implement a receive queue for the mode switch notifications
of each mode machine instance.⌋
In contrast to the event communication, for mode switch communication, the length
is associated with the sender side, the mode manager, because it is unique for the
mode machine instance.
[SWS_Rte_08941] Queue length for the mode manager side
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00143
⌈The RTE shall determine the queue length for the mode manager side according to
the following priority rules (upmost in the list goes first):
1. value of the ECU-C parameter RteModeSenderQueueLength
2. value of the queueLength attribute of the ModeSwitchSenderComSpec
⌋
[SWS_Rte_02719]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107, SRS_Rte_00110
⌈The mode switch notification shall be written to the end of the queue and
read (consuming) from the front of the queue (i.e. the queue is first-in-first-out).⌋
[SWS_Rte_02720]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00107, SRS_Rte_00110
⌈If a new mode switch notification is received when the queue is already filled,
the RTE shall discard the received notification.⌋
In this case, Rte_Switch will return an error, see [SWS_Rte_02675].
